text:
Jacob Trouba is in his fourth NHL home, San Jose, after parts of two seasons in Anaheim, and the Sharks are leaning on him hard: 22 minutes a night, 43 hits and 37 blocked shots in 24 games. After the Nov. 17 loss to Calgary he was the one at the podium, and Sportsnaut's headline summed up his read: "Not Our Best Game."

The team around him spends a lot of time in its own end. San Jose gets about 46% of both the shot attempts and the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five. That's poor, but it's nearly three points better than the Sharks manage without him, which is the case for playing a veteran on a young team.

Last season's numbers were harder on him: Evolving-Hockey had him below replacement level. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows both sides of his game. He stops 16% of the entries aimed at him (typical 11%), but only 28% of his exits keep possession. Watch the breakouts. When the forecheck comes, that's where his shifts get long.
